location.name: Nukunonu
location.role: Atoll named geographic entity; source-family candidate includes the atoll’s emergent dry land, not a settlement or political ownership claim. Keep one location for the atoll subject; do not create each islet as a location without scale-policy review.
location.settlement_assessment: Tokelau Government describes two main settlements, connected by a concrete bridge; Fale is the main village and Motuhaga a more recent settlement. Their built-up footprints are not separate atoll locations. Official page is historical and cites 2006 census population (426), not current population evidence.
location.proposed_correction: Retain named-atoll granularity as a proposed geographic location. Repair its reference footprint from a versioned, auditable shoreline family only after independent validation of completeness/shoreline policy. No hierarchy or geometry edit in this packet.
unresolved: Independent authoritative modern coastline family/completeness and tide/reef interpretation are not certified.
OSM labels/places identify some named islets; official source describes the atoll and settlements but does not enumerate all 97 dry-land components.
Current Atlas boundary treatment for lagoon, reef, reef-flat, and unnamed motu requires engineering geospatial review.

source.name: OpenStreetMap coastline ways, Tokelau/Nukunonu map extract
source.license: Open Database License 1.0 (ODbL); attribution © OpenStreetMap contributors; share-alike obligations apply to adapted database.
source.method: Use archived OSM API map response; select natural=coastline ways in the issue bbox; reconstruct complete rings from source node references and measure the full rings without clipping. Existing repository osm-report.json records the full family-level land-ring reconstruction and absent-footprint comparison. This packet verifier independently checks archive and ring topology.
source.source_versioning: Per-way versions and timestamps are inventoried; extract retrieved 2026-10-02. Current source state does not establish the date the coast physically formed or historical effective dates.
source.limitations: Query bbox is a retrieval envelope, not a legal or approved geographic boundary. OSM community-mapped coastline is not authoritative title or sovereign evidence. OSM family appears exhaustive within the extract; independent modern coastline agreement remains unresolved.

official_sources.publication_date: Not stated; page content includes 2013 figures and strategic-plan text from 2010–2015

official_sources.findings: Tokelau comprises three coral atolls; Nukunonu is central, reported area 4.7 km²; reefs/sands/rock, 3–5 m above sea level. Political description is kept separate from geographic role.

official_sources.publication_date: Not stated; Nukunonu population data explicitly references 2001 and 2006 censuses
official_sources.license: Copyright Government of Tokelau; no open reuse license stated. No page bytes redistributed.
official_sources.findings: Two main settlements: Fale and Motuhaga; joined by a concrete bridge. Motuhaga is described as recent and site of St Joseph hospital. Official narrative supports settlement completeness at named-village level but is dated; census population 426 is for 2006.

audit.current_world_index_assessment: Source profile says Atlas parent chain is location → Tokelau province → Tokelau Archipelago area → Western Polynesian Islands region → Polynesia → Oceania. Existing wider Tokelau location represents Atafu/Fakaofo and does not contain this named atoll; sibling parents are intentionally unchanged.

historical_comparison_context.interpretation: Preserved pre-restoration comparison only; do not read its zero-overlap values as current indexed coverage.

audit.current_coverage_status: Current geometry overlap is measured separately; the indexed source feature is not a hierarchy node or geographic approval.
audit.archived_pre_restoration_independent_gsh: Repository comparison found 21 complete level-1 GSHHG polygons totaling 4.833268655 km²; all 21 partially match OSM dry-land components, 0% of the query-selected source polygons are currently represented in atlas region. Different total area/partition (OSM 5.482223456 km²) means shoreline/generalization differences; GSHHG source vintage and policy resolution needed before treating as exact completeness verdict. Each polygon bbox/ID/count/overlap status recorded below.
audit.current_gshhg_assessment: Current indexed overlap is in current-coverage.json; it does not establish complete or suitable modern shoreline geometry.

ownership_history: No sovereignty, owner, historical affiliation, or effective-time attribute is inferred from geographic containment or administrative vocabulary. Tokelau Government political description is contextual only.

province_assessment.current_role: single-child named territory/province reference parent, open semantic/boundary review
province_assessment.issue_scope: one owned location of current two; the other member is outside this issue
province_assessment.finding: A Tokelau territorial administrative label is plausible from official governance source, but this packet does not establish a complete legal province polygon, date-valid administrative boundary, or semantic appropriateness of a standalone single-child province tier. Tokelau consists of three separated atolls; this issue covers only Nukunonu and cannot assess the full parent.
province_assessment.recommendation: Retain unchanged for now; coordinate a full-parent review across both members and the separate Tokelau Archipelago area before any parent or child chain correction. No province geometry/membership change proposed here.

area_assessment.current_role: physical archipelago reference grouping; three current locations, one owned here
area_assessment.finding: Tokelau consists of three separated atolls, consistent with a named archipelago grouping in broad geographic terms. Exact shared-parent footprint, semantic tier, and neighbor partition remain open at the whole-area level, outside this one-member scope.
area_assessment.recommendation: No change; combined original-plus-supplemental regional integration must review all three members and all original evidence.
